correctness.rationale: The 36 normalized profiles exhaust all 216 labeled three-agent strict profiles by a free six-house relabeling action. For each profile all six bijections, 36 ordered majority comparisons, six direct Pareto checks and McKelvey covering predicates are exhaustive. The explicit complete table gives 7 joint atoms and exactly 108 profiles with nonzero TC-minus-PO difference; direct and independent per-profile algorithms agree on sets in all 216 cases. Two-agent minimality follows by considering the only two bijections. All quantifiers and finite domain boundaries are given; no infinite proof is inferred.

originality.rationale: The natural first nontrivial assignment-majority market is analyzed in the 2026 primary source only via possible top-cycle sizes. Its available section on uncovered-set frequencies enumerates five-agent markets, not the full 216-profile three-agent joint law. The 2017 majority-graph study counts graph types, not the three set cardinalities and their joint law. Existing three-agent serial-dictatorship probability-shape results are not equivalent to Pareto inefficiency of the majority top cycle. Searches for these aliases and implications found no matching full seven-atom census. Residual priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The exact probability 1/2 and conditional {1,2,3} uniform severity quantify the economic risk of majority-based top-cycle choice in the smallest square assignment market permitting Pareto inefficiency. Jointly classifying Pareto efficiency and the McKelvey refinement connects three substantively motivated objects, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The original majoritarian assignment analysis explicitly studies efficiency of top cycles and discriminating uncovered sets but lacks these three-agent frequencies. The finite law is independently meaningful without an extension to larger electorates.
